title: Suspected stroke at a care home
setting: Local care home. 74M resident is sitting in a chair, slurring his words. Drooped face on one side and cannot lift his left arm.
verdictExplanation: Positive FAST test (Face drooped, Arm weakness, Speech slurred). This is a suspected stroke, a time-critical neurological emergency. Sick: requires immediate 999 escalation.

shared.response: Alert but confused and slurring speech

history.history: Symptom onset 15 minutes ago while sitting at a table
history.additional: Staff are extremely concerned as he was talking normally minutes ago

followUp.question: What is your immediate priority management for this suspected stroke?

options.text: Call 999 immediately, note exact onset time, keep calm, and protect the airway
Give him a sugary drink to treat a potential hypoglycaemic episode
Give him his ramipril tablet to lower his high blood pressure
Encourage him to lie flat and sleep, checking on him in an hour

followUp.explanation: Suspected stroke is a medical emergency. Call 999 immediately and record exact onset time for thrombolysis. Do not give anything by mouth due to swallowing risk. Sleep is dangerous as it delays time-sensitive care.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Perform FAST test, call 999 immediately, and record time of onset.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected acute stroke. Monitor airway (risk of aspiration), check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycaemia (mimics stroke), provide oxygen if indicated, and prepare for rapid transport.
